# Temple Scroll Column 34 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 34 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**34:1** And the chambers that are on the west side of the outer court shall be for the sons of Israel who come up to the temple to worship before Me.

**34:2** And they shall bring their offerings and their sacrifices and their vows and their freewill offerings.

**34:3** And they shall eat them in these chambers — they and their sons and their daughters and their menservants and their maidservants.

**34:4** And no stranger shall eat of the holy things, for it is not permitted to him.

**34:5** And the priests shall eat of the most holy things within the inner court; and the holy things they shall eat in the chambers that are appointed to them in the outer court.

**34:6** Each man in his appointed place shall eat; they shall not mix one with another.

**34:7** And the priests shall not go out from their chambers carrying any of the holy food to the outer court.

**34:8** And they shall not profane My holy food; for it is holy, and they shall treat it as holy.

**34:9** And any man of the sons of Israel who brings a sacrifice — he shall come to the gate that is nearest to him.

**34:10** And the Levites shall receive it from his hand at the gate; and they shall bring it to the priests at the altar.

**34:11** And each man shall come with his offering to the gate that is appointed for his tribe.

**34:12** And he shall not enter through the gate of another tribe; for each tribe has its own gate.

**34:13** And the sons of Levi shall stand at the gates to receive the offerings from the hand of the sons of Israel.

**34:14** And they shall carry them to the altar and to the chambers, each offering to its proper place.

**34:15** And no man shall come into the outer court empty-handed before Me at the appointed feasts.

**34:16** Each man shall bring according to his ability — according to the blessing of the LORD his God that He has given him.

---

*EMET notes: Column 34 regulates tribal access through assigned gates and the flow of offerings from layperson to Levite to priest. The prohibition against entering through another tribe's gate is distinctive to 11QT. The language of v. 16 echoes Deuteronomy 16:17.*
